newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand hopes to make more bond issues - Amnuay.
newsitem.headline: Thailand hopes to make more bond issues - Amnuay.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday the government was in the process of amending a law so it will be able to issue more government bonds to raise money to fund state enterprise projects.

"The government is working to amend laws to allow it to issue more bonds even though it still enjoys a budget surplus," Amnuay told reporters after speaking to a conference on the outlook of the bond market.
Under current law, the government cannot issue government bonds while it has a budget surplus.
Amnuay said the bond issues would be used to help finance state enteprise projects.
He also said the government wants to promote more issues of both public sector and private sector bonds as part of a policy to mobilise long-term savings which would promote economic stability.
Amnuay also said the government was observing the market reaction to Wednesday's one billion baht launch of seven-year, zero-coupon bonds to decide when to issue further tranches.
The central bank said on Wednesday the auction results would be known in the afternoon.
"A seven-year, zero-coupon bond in principal should normally yield a coupon of about nine percent," Amnuay said.
The auction is the first tranche of bonds to be sold of a total issue of 50 billion baht in zero-coupon bonds.
Proceeds of the bonds would be used to purchase non-performing property loans from banks and finance companies, aiding cash-strapped property firms.
The bond issue is to be managed by the government-run Property Loans Management Organisation (PLMO).
